title.narrative: Joint Executive Program Reducing child mortality due to pneumonia by increasing access to medical oxygen in a humanitarian setting in Somalia

description.narrative: 1- Reducing the mortality of premature babies, children and adults. 2- Providing medications for chronic diseases 3- Equipping 25 solar-powered oxygen stations 4- Providing medical devices and equipment in 25 medical units 1,000,000 beneficiaries benefited from the project.

Alleviating the suffering of the Somali citizen by providing the necessary medicines for his treatment and the treatment of family members, especially women and children. - Supporting the resilience of the health sector in Somalia and preventing its collapse. - Increasing the number of births by providing incubators for needy cases

Child mortality rates in Somalia are among the highest in the world. A child born today in Somalia is 16.5 times more likely to die before the age of five than any other child anywhere else. The mortality rate for children under the age of five in Somalia is currently 117 per 1,000 live births. About 21% of these deaths among children under the age of five in Somalia are attributed to pneumonia. This project aims to operate more than 10 medical oxygen stations in various places in Somalia, in addition to Providing medicines to treat pneumonia patients
